Annually, initiatives are undertaken to support young nutrition scientists from developing countries, enabling them to attend international scientific meetings and participate in capacity development activities, such as workshops on nutrition leadership. 2. The foundation's primary purpose is to support research, education, and science within German universities. Additionally, it contributes to charitable and humanitarian organizations. No commercially operating companies are involved in the foundation's operations, either directly or indirectly. 3. Professor Elmadfa's declared interests were not considered to constitute any conflict of interest regarding his role as a member of the NUGAG Subgroup on Diet and Health, nor did they represent any conflict of interest for the work being undertaken by the subgroup. 4. Dr. Lee Hooper disclosed that she received research funding from Barry Callebaut (to her university) to conduct a systematic review on the effects of chocolate and cocoa on markers of oxidative stress, which was completed in August 2010. She also received research funding from the Soy Nutrition Institute (to her university) to carry out a systematic review on the effects of soy and isoflavones on hormonal status in women, completed in July 2008. Additionally, Dr. Hooper received a plane ticket and hotel accommodation from the European Hydration Institute (EHI) during her participation at the 20th IUNS International Congress of Nutrition in Granada, Spain, in September 2013, where she was an invited speaker at the EHI’s symposium. Her talk focused on dehydration in older people. She received no personal remuneration other than the travel and accommodation noted above. 5. Although Dr. Hooper's declared interests were unrelated to the guidelines on free sugars in relation to weight gain and dental caries, she did not participate in discussions or work of the NUGAG Subgroup on Diet and Health related to these guidelines. It was agreed that her declared interests did not constitute any conflict of interest for her participation in other ongoing work of the subgroup, including updating the guidelines on fats and fatty acids. 6. Professor Nahla Hwalla declared that she has received research support, including grants, collaborations, sponsorships, and other funding from WHO, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), the Lebanese National Council for Scientific Research, the UN University (UNU), and Nestlé Middle East. Further information revealed that the grant from Nestlé Middle East supports two types of projects at the American University of Beirut (AUB): intervention activities promoting healthy eating in schools and research activities by three faculty members in the Faculty of Agriculture and Food Sciences, overseen by Professor Hwalla as the Dean of the Faculty. An agreement between AUB and Nestlé Middle East ensures that all intellectual property produced during the projects belongs to AUB. 7. It was agreed that Professor Hwalla could participate as a member of the NUGAG Subgroup on Diet and Health, as her interest is not personal, the amount received is not significant relative to the faculty's total budget, and the funding supports a pre-existing program with governmental support. An appropriate disclosure statement was suggested to indicate her declared interest. 8. Professor Mary L’Abbé declared that she received research grants from the Canadian Institutes of Health Research to evaluate the impact of Canada’s sodium reduction policy, the Public Health Agency of Canada to prepare a report on public food procurement policies related to sodium, and the Beef Information Centre to examine the iron bioavailability of Canadian diets. She also receives funding for research in NCD prevention and health promotion. Professor L’Abbé has spoken at the annual meeting of the Canadian Meat Council to explain Canada’s Sodium Working Group report recommendations and the process for developing Canada’s sodium targets for foods. Her travel expenses were paid by the Canadian Meat Council, but no honorarium was received. 9. Professor L’Abbé appeared as a witness to the Canadian Parliament’s Standing Committee on Health, advocating for action to reduce sodium in Canadian foods, increase consumer awareness of sodium, and support research in the sodium field. The research grant from the Beef Information Centre was unrelated to the recommendations being reviewed and updated by the NUGAG Subgroup on Diet and Health. It was suggested that her declared interest be reported in the process and meeting report with details, but no action was required, and she was accepted as a member of the subgroup. 10. Dr. Anna Lartey declared that her department runs a short course on food safety for nutritionists, supported by the Industry Council for Development, a non-profit organization with official relations with WHO and liaison status with FAO. This organization aims to improve public health worldwide through the development of projects and learning resources on food safety. Its website provides access to training materials on food safety, HACCP, risk analysis and assessment, and drinking water quality. It was considered that her declared interests do not constitute any conflict of interest for her role as a member of the NUGAG Subgroup on Diet and Health. 11. Professor Jim Mann declared that he is employed by a university with an interest in nutrition as it relates to human health and receives research grants from New Zealand governmental agencies. He has provided expert advice on nutrition and human health to numerous national and international bodies, including WHO, FAO, the World Cancer Research Fund, and the media. His declared interests were not considered to constitute any conflict of interest for his role as a member of the NUGAG Subgroup on Diet and Health. 12. Professor Satoshi Sasaki declared that he received an air ticket, hotel accommodation, and a small lecture fee from Ajinomoto Co. for his participation in a scientific meeting held in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, in March 2013. It was considered that his declared interests do not constitute any conflict of interest for his role as a member of the NUGAG Subgroup on Diet and Health. 13. Professor Barbara Schneeman declared that, until the end of 2012, she was employed by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), which is interested in scientific input for developing nutrition recommendations. She also served as the US delegate to the Codex Committees on food labeling and on nutrition and foods for special dietary uses, representing the US position in these forums. Additionally, she served as a consultant to Exponent, a consulting firm, providing information on FDA policies for labeling genetically engineered plant ingredients and nutrient content claims. She gave a presentation on the development of the Dietary Guidelines for Americans and US nutrition labeling policies at the Mushroom Council, a Commodity Board supported by mushroom growers. Her declared interests were not considered to constitute any conflict of interest for her role as a member of the NUGAG Subgroup on Diet and Health. 14. Professor Murray Skeaff declared that he was invited to an international symposium on reducing saturated fat intake in cardiovascular disease prevention, organized by the University of Copenhagen. Travel, accommodation, and honorarium were funded by the Opus Centre and the Centre of Advanced Food Research. He withdrew his name from the meeting consensus statement upon learning of the involvement of commercial interests. He also declared memberships in various advisory groups, including the Public Health Scientific Advisory Group of the New Zealand National Heart Foundation, the Food and Nutrition Working Group of the Heart Foundation, and the New Zealand Food Safety Academy. None of these roles involve remuneration. His declared interests were not considered to constitute any conflict of interest for his role as a member of the NUGAG Subgroup on Diet and Health. 15. Professor (Esté) Vorster declared that she serves on the Scientific Panel advising the South African Sugar Association (SASA) on nutrition research funding at South African universities. She stated that serving on the panel does not commit her to support any policy or viewpoint of SASA, and she receives no financial benefits. SASA promotes the global competitiveness and sustainability of the South African sugar industry. However, a statement on SASA’s website about sugar and health contradicts WHO guidance and the work of the NUGAG Subgroup on Diet and Health. It was suggested that Professor Vorster could continue as a member of the subgroup but should refrain from participating in discussions and decision-making on free sugars recommendations. She could fully participate in discussions on other topics, such as fats and fatty acids.
